title: «THE AMERICAN DREAM» AND «ACHIEVING SOCIALISM» AS COMPETING CULTURAL CODES IN THE COLD WAR ERA
abstract: The article is devoted to a comparative cultural analysis of two competing symbolic models of the desired future, formed in the USA and the USSR during the Cold War era, which are considered in the study as stable cultural codes structuring social expectations, value and anthropological attitudes of mass consciousness. The focus is on comparing the “American dream” and the ideal of “achieving socialism” as two different ways of articulating happiness, success and the meaning of human life in the context of global ideological confrontation. It is consistently proved that the American dream was based on an individualistic logic that presupposes the achievability of success within the existing social order, whereas the Soviet project was based on a collectivist and utopian view of the possibility of moral transformation of man and the construction of a classless society in a historical perspective. The article analyzes the evolution of the socialist ideal from an early amorphous utopia to more materialistically oriented forms ofthe late Soviet period, which led to its partial convergence with the consumer attitudes of the American dream and at the same time to the loss of the internal

title: PERSONIFICATION IN THE FIGURATIVE AND SEMANTIC STRUCTURE OF A STATE HOLIDAY
abstract: The article is devoted to the study of the potential and mechanisms of including a character in the context of a state holiday as a key condition for actualizing the event, consolidating and revitalizing «invented traditions», as well as ensuring the continuity of generations. The article analyzes various types of characters, proposes a clear distinction between the concepts of «hero» and «character», and determines the functional role of personification in the figurative and semantic structure of a state holiday. Special attention is paid to the development and presentation of a consistent algorithm for integrating a character into the process of «generalizing» a festive event, which allows for a systematic approach to its design and implementation. As a result of the study, it is concluded that a character is one of the necessary conditions for a full-fledged «life» of a holiday and an effective tool for involving participants in it, contributing to its dynamic development and maintaining its semantic depth. The study uses methods of exemplification, design, and analysis, which allowed for a comprehensive examination of the problem and the development of practical solutions.

title: CULTUROLOGY AS CRYPTANALYSIS: TO THE PROBLEM OF METHODS OF DECODING MEMORIAL SPACES
abstract: The article explores the concept of «cultural code», which has recently become widespread in various Russian discourses. The purpose of the work is to substantiate the methodological paradigm that considers cultural studies as a form of «cryptanalysis» and to develop a general algorithm for decoding the semantic layers of memorial spaces. The methods of cryptanalysis (frequency and mathematical), semiotics, cultural memory, and spatial theory are used as a theoretical starting point. Comparative analysis, structural and semantic decoding, and polyphonic interpretation of sources are used as methodological tools. The empirical part is based on the study of the memorial landscape of Arkaim as a case demonstrating the interaction of symbolic representations, material culture and practices of remembrance. The results of the study include the formalization of procedures for identifying levels of the “cultural code”, the identification of typological categories of iconic complexes, and the description of mechanisms for their translation into public memory. The work shows that, despite the metaphorical nature of the term “cryptanalysis,” this approach makes it possibleto systematize metho

title: SECULAR SACREDNESS: CONCEPT AND SOCIOCULTURAL PRACTICES
abstract: This article examines secular sacredness as an independent and self-sufficient phenomenon of the modern sociocultural space. The content and specificity of secular sacredness are analyzed in comparison with the religious manifestations of this phenomenon. It is established that the secular mode of sacredness includes the activity of a subject belong to the immanent world. This gives rise to a unique process of sacralization of object in real sociocultural spheres, embodied in a variety of variants. In accordance with the characteristics of secular sacralization, it forms a distinctive transcendence as a sphere of existence for sublime images conveying the value- semantic significance of objects sacralized in secular space. The independent existence of secular sacredness does not preclude its interaction with religious sacredness, giving rise to various combinations of the two. Verification of the theoretical presented in the text was carried out through reference to systemic (“civil religion”), artifactual (Eternal Flame) and activity-based (state national holiday) variants of the embodiment of secular sacredness in sociocultural practices.

title: THE GENESIS AND TRANSFORMATION OF THE AUTHOR`S THEATERIN THE CONTEXT OF THE REGIONAL CULTURAL ENVIRONMENT (BASED ON THE CITY OF CHELYABINSK)
abstract: This article explores the phenomenon of auteur theater as a radical art form within the specific cultural environment of an industrial region. Using an analysis of theatrical life in Chelyabinsk, the author traces the genesis of avant-garde movements, determined by a complex set of sociocultural factors. Particular attention is paid to the cyclical development of the regional theater space, characterized by alternating phases of stagnation and renewal. Nikolai Borisov’s project “Very Bad Theater” is used as an example, representing a contemporary model of auteur artistic protest. The study identifies the mechanisms by which elite art adapts to regional sociocultural conditions and demonstrates how the institutional system absorbs and neutralizes radical artistic practices during the process of their legitimization.

title: EFFECTIVE SOUND - STIMULATING CONSUMPTION IN MODERN CULTURE THROUGH MUSIC
abstract: The article examines the features of the pragmatic use of music in modern culture in order to stimulate the consumption ofgoods and services. For this purpose, the text examines and interprets the functional and applied methods of music application that preceded today’s practices (Eric Satie’s “Furniture” music and Muzak background music), identifies the characteristic features of music distribution using modern technologies, and highlights the specifics of current forms of individual listening to music and its use for personal purposes using the example of the digital music streaming service Yandex Music, identifies and analyzes the key features of the utilitarian use of music in order to stimulate the consumption of goods and services through specialized digital services for commercial use Sound Business and Cube Media. The author of the article adheres to an interdisciplinary cultural approach, applying the results and provisions of humanitarian research in his work, which are devoted to the study of the role of music and sound in culture, uses general scientific methods of analysis, comparison, generalization and synthesis, and also adheres to the principle of integrity when co

title: THE ONTOLOGY OF THE ETERNAL CARNIVAL:FESTIVE MONSTROSITY AND STRUCTURAL LACK OF THE SUBJECT IN THE FEYWILD MODEL
abstract: The article analyzes the transformation of festive culture in the 21st century and the emergence of the «festive monstrosity» phenomenon. The study aims to identify the mechanisms that turn the liminal space of celebration into an invasive environment that suppresses the participant’s subjectivity. The theoretical framework relies on J. Baudrillard’s concept of hyperreality, M. Bakhtin’s theory of carnival, and V. Propp’s morphology of the folktale. The methodology employs a synthesis of structural-semiotic analysis of game rules and a praxeological analysis of subject interaction models within algorithmic environments. The research is based on the Dungeons & Dragons campaign module The Wild Beyond the Witchlight, including the prelude adventure «Lost Things».The analysis reveals that the game’s narrative structure reproduces the initial functions of the fairy tale but blocks the phase of affliction liquidation, constructing a «myth of trauma» and establishing a normative lack of self. It is determined that monstrosityin this model manifests through the alienation of qualia - intimate personal properties. The study identifies specific agency recovery strategies -»normative groundin

title: THE UNIVERSAL PICTURE OF THE WORLD AS A PORTAL FOR GHOSTS
abstract: Ghosts are a traditional element of any worldview. They create the plot of literary works, dreams, and even possess the ability to intervene in the course of historical events. Despite their diversity, they all come from the past, revealing it to the present.The authors of the article believe that ghosts inhabit the social relations of the metaphysical, dialectical, electromagnetic, relativistic, quantum, and postmodern worldviews. Each is characterized by its own mode of thinking and objective activity. This mode is a kind of medium, whose consciousness leaves an imprint on the spirit it evokes.In the mechanical worldview, ghosts affirmed the justice of legal laws; in the dialectical worldview, they affirmed the specificity of romantic consciousness; in the electromagnetic worldview, mediums summoned spirits; in the relativistic worldview, ghosts helped relive aristocratic life; in the quantum worldview, counts were replaced by extraterrestrial intelligence.To become a subject of social relations, a person must internalize the entire history of civilization, which they bring to the object of their relationship. title: HISTORICAL AND CULTURAL FACTORS IN THE FORMATION AND DEVELOPMENT OF THE ORENBURG DOWN-KNITTING INDUSTRY (XVIII-XX CENTURIES)
abstract: This article presents a comprehensive cultural analysis of the key factors that shaped the formation and development of the Orenburg down-knitting industry, considered a unique phenomenon of Russian material culture. Unlike studies focusing on technological or artistic aspects, this work identifies and systematizes the historical and cultural determinants that contributed to the transformation of a local craft into a national brand. Drawing on historical, ethnographic, and local history sources, the author identifies four main stages and corresponding factors.These include: 1) the ethnographic factor of cross-cultural exchange (mid-18th century), based on the adoption by the Orenburg Cossacks (primarily Cossack women) of the collection and processing of goat wool from nomadic peoples and their synthesis with Russian knitting techniques; 2) the state-administrative factor (second half of the 18th century), associated with the scientificdescription of the down-knitting industry in the Orenburg province by P. title: THE LIMITS OF CULTURAL DIALOGUE IN THE INFORMATION AGE:USER CONTENT BETWEEN ATOMIZATION AND SELF-REFERENCE
abstract: This article presents an attempt at a culturological analysis of existing digital cultural phenomena, particularly user-generated content, and their influence on the development and structure of contemporary culture. Using Yuri Lotman's approach to analyzing cultural phenomena, the author examines the consequences of the popularity and potential influence on the cultural dynamics of the Minecraft video game, as well as the user-generated content created by video bloggers using this video game. The author concludes that the high variability of user-generated content, coupled with the already high variability of cultural phenomena, can influence the format and productivity of dialogue as the primary mean of generating new cultural phenomena. An attempt is made to interpret the change in dialogue format within the framework of the intersubjective-intrasubjective dichotomy.

title: THE SCENARIO MATRIX OF A STATE HOLIDAY: NEW OR FORGOTTEN OLD?
abstract: The article examines the evolution of the scenario matrix of state holidays as a tool of symbolic politics and the construction of national identity. The author introduces the concept of a “scenario matrix,” defining it as a stable model for organizing a celebration, encompassing narrative, semiotic, communicative, and spatio-temporal elements. Based on an analysis of holiday scenarios implemented in Chelyabinsk between 2016 and 2025, and employing content and narrative analysis, the study identifies key trends in the transformation of festive culture. The results demonstrate a shift from a purely commemorative nature of holidays to a mobilizational one: a sharp increase in the proportion of current political elements, the dominance of the local (ethno-cultural) identity vector over the universal one, a rise in the frequency of state symbolism use, and the increasing complexity of formats (multi-format, immersive experiences). The evolution of the narrative (from historical reconstruction to mobilizational synthesis) and theritual-ceremonial component is analyzed separately. title: NATIONAL HOLIDAYS AS AN INSTRUMENT OF “SOFT POWER” AND THE FORMATION OF THE INTERNATIONAL IMAGE OF THE STATE
abstract: This article analyzes the role of national holidays as a tool for shaping a state’s international image and implementing the concept of “soft power.” In the context of globalization and increasing intercultural ties, a country’s positive image is becoming an important factor in international relations. In this article, we examine how national holidays can contribute to strengthening cultural diplomacy, shaping and communicating national identity, and improving a state’s image on the global stage. We focus on the mechanisms by which holidays help disseminate examples of national culture, break down stereotypes, and strengthen ties between peoples. We also examine a number of challenges associated with the dissemination of national holidays for people with a migration history within the cultural field of the host society and the need for intercultural dialogue to achieve harmony in multinational communities. The article emphasizes that the effective use of national holidays requires a strategic approach, as well as consideration of cultural characteristics and universal values.

title: ON THE STATUS OF PARALITERATURE IN METAMODERNISM
abstract: The article examines paraliterature as a sociocultural practice within metamodernism, as a new episteme characterized by oscillation. The study aims to explore the nature, functions, and specificity of paraliterature against the backdrop of shifting cultural hierarchies and the digitization of culture. The research material includes theoretical works on paraliterature as well as empirical examples of non-institutional writing (texts published on self-publishing platforms and produced in creative writing schools). The methodological framework draws on cultural studies, Michel Foucault’s concept of discursive formation, and Richard Saint-Gelais’s notion of “transfictionality.” The discussion emphasizes that while paraliterature originated within postmodernism, it has acquired new forms in the metamodern era due to digital technologies and a shift in emphasis from aesthetic value toward communicative and identity-forming functions. The author concludes that paraliterature constitutes an autonomous, marginal yet viable sector of contemporary culture, where legitimacy is conferred not by institutions but by community practices, and where value resides not in artistic quality but in part

title: THE RUSSIAN NATIONAL COSTUME IN THE SPACE OF STATE HOLIDAY:ANALYSIS OF CURRENT PRACTICES
abstract: The article analyses the functions and meanings acquired by the Russian national costume within the ritualised space of contemporary Russian state holidays. The author considers this process as a deliberate element of state cultural policy aimed at consolidating society and providing a visual representation of symbols that unify the nation. The empirical basis of the study is a narrative analysis of posts from the official website of the Ministry of Culture of the Russian Federation over a five-year period.The main findings of the work point to a consistent trend of the purposeful incorporation of folk costume, especially during holidays of historical and political significance (Russia Day, National Unity Day, Victory Day). The costume plays a dual role: on the one hand, it serves as a demarcating sign of cultural distinctiveness and “spiritual bonds,” and on the other, it acts as an integrating element visualising the unity of a multinational people. The author identifies key forms of the costume’s utilisation (flash mobs, theatricalperformances, immersive installations) and differentiates its roles (key/background, focused/participatory).The article argues that within the context

title: THE ROLE OF MILITARY CULTURE IN FORMING THE SEMANTIC FIELDOF RUSSIAN STATE HOLIDAYS AND THE SYMBOLIC CONSOLIDATION OF SOCIETY
abstract: The significance of the army’s institutional role in the country’s historical development cannot be overstated. The army has always played a vital role in the formation and strengthening of the state, ensuring its security, and preserving its territorial integrity. In the modern world, its influence extends not only to the political and military spheres but also to the sociocultural space, especially in a country with a rich historical tradition like Russia. Today, the projection of military culture into the Russian sociocultural space has powerful potential for shaping the national and cultural identity of citizens. Military history, the exploits of ancestors, and significant victories serve as an important symbolic resource, strengthening a sense of patriotism and belonging to the state. National holidays dedicated to military victories and the courage of ancestors are a special tool for shaping national memory. They convey important images, meanings, and values, creating a patriotic foundation for the education of citizens. Days of Military Glory and memorable dates in Russia occupy a special place in this process. Ceremonial events such as military parades, troop marches, naval

title: ARKAIM AS AN EXPERIENCED SPACE:AN ANALYSIS OF PERCEPTION THROUGH VISITORS’ OPEN STATEMENTS
abstract: This article examines the perception of the Arkaim Museum-Reserve based on the open statements of its visitors. The study examines Arkaim as an experienced space using five aspects of open statements: 1) the frequency of vocabulary used and its thematic categorization, 2) psychological assessment, 3) comparative description of space, 4) the characteristic of space used, and 5) narrativization of space. The use of these aspects is based on a phenomenological approach, humanitarian geography, and semantic analysis. Each aspectof the analysis allows us to consider how a neutral space is transformed into an experienced place imbued with individual and collective meaning. The analysis shows that the dominant semantic fields form a stable configuration of perception, in which the historical aspect of the space is inextricably linked with the natural landscape and the collective sense of the space’s spirituality. Analogies in descriptions of the sensations of being at Arkaim also confirm the appeal to Arkaim’s significance and its spirituality. The characteristics of the space in visitors’ comments also capture the connection between the historical and spiritual aspects of the space. Arka

title: ARTISTIC SYMBOLICS AND ELEGIAC PLOT IN THE POEM “AUTUMN IN THE PARK” BY BORIS RYZHY
abstract: The article examines the poetics of Boris Ryzhy’s poem “Autumn in the Park”, which clearly shows the key features of the poet’s creative thinking. The reflexive understanding of the dichotomy of life and death and the elegiac perception of contemporary reality, which appear as peculiar constants of his lyrics, reveal various ways and forms of their verbal actualization. One of such conceptually significant embodiments of B. Ryzhy’s poetic “elegism” is his reflection on the “autumn-park” realities projected into the microcosm of the lyrical hero. The structural-semiotic and phenomenological approaches used to study the poetic text help to clarify the verbalization of elegy in the poet’s work. An analytical review of the poem “Autumn in the Park” testifies to the semantic unity of artistic symbolism and plot structure of the text. This work demonstrates the lyrical hero’s immersion in a reflexive understanding of death as a marker of the progressive abolition of existential vitality. Regret for the passing of life produces the elegiac character of reflexive comprehension of the ontological presence of man in the world. title: THE RUIN AS AN IMAGE AND A MEDIUM OF MEMORY(BORIS RYZHY’S POEM «WHAT CAN BE SAID ABOUT MARBLE - I AM IN LOVE WITH RUINS...»)
abstract: The article analyzes Boris Ryzhy’s poem «What Can Be Said about Marble - I Am in Love with Ruins…» from the perspective of the poetics of the visual image and cultural memory. The focus is on the image of the ruin, considered not merely as a motif or an object of representation, but as a medium of memory that determines the unfolding of the lyric plot and the organization of the poem’s semantic structure. The analysis combines a structural approach to the poetic text with the theory of cultural memory and also takes into account the aesthetic concept of the ruin in the European philosophical and artistic tradition.The study demonstrates that the image of the ruin in Ryzhy’s poem performs a structuring function, linking visual and verbal planes, individual experience and cultural memory, past and present. Particular attention is paid to the subject structure of the text, to transformations of the image of the creative idea (thought), and to intermedial transitions between sculpture and poetry. title: COLLABORATION WITH THE ROCK GROUPS “NAUTILUS POMPILIUS” AND “NASTYA” AS AN OPTION FOR SELF-REFLECTION IN THE WORKS OF ILYA KORMILTSEV
abstract: The article examines the phenomenon of literary self-reflection on the example of Ilya Kormiltsev’s work. In understanding the phenomenon of self-reflection in literature, the author of the article relies on the research of O.Yu. Antsyferova and M.P. Abasheva. The material for the study was the texts written by the poet for the rock bands Nautilus Pompilius and Nastya, which have not previously been analyzed and compared in a single study. It has been established that Kormiltsev was an author who was prone to various forms of self-reflection: through the self-knowledge of lyrical subjects, the evaluation of their creative output, and the scientific analysis of his own works. Kormiltsev’s collaboration with the Nautilus Pompilius band lasted much longer than his collaboration with the Nastya band, he only worked together with these two groups for one year. As a result, a number of motifs that first appeared in the lyrics for one band could then be incorporated into the lyrics for the other band and further developed. title: LYRICS BY KSENIA NEKRASOVA: FEATURES OF THE POETIC STYLE
abstract: Ksenia Nekrasova’s artistic world is based on a sense of connection between everything. She acts not as the creator of poetic reality, but as a chronicler, putting into texts everything she sees around her: “If you listen to how Russian people talk and write letters, you can insert them into the chapters of poems without correction”. Ksenia Nekrasova sees the great in the small, emphasizing the importance of all living things - this is a distinctive feature of her poetic style. This can manifest itself in the selection of images and themes, and then the reader’s interest is supported by the unusual color palette, metaphors, and epithets. Let us emphasize the unexpected but organic connection between the poetics of Ksenia Nekrasova’s landscape and the poetics of the oriental landscape. With a sense of joy, quivering feeling to nature, Ksenia Nekrasova listens, looks into the world around her with a truly Tyutchev pantheism - into her soul, freedom, language, love. However, the language does not always suit her, and then she begins her word-making. title: PERM REGION AS A CONFLICTED ARTISTIC SPACE (THE GEOPOETICS OF ANDREI RODIONOV AND EKATERINA TROEPOLSKAYA’S PLAY “HAPPINESS IS JUST AROUND THE CORNER”)
abstract: The fact that the Ural space is a posteriori conflictual has been repeatedly acknowledged historically and aesthetically (we can recall numerous examples, from the circumstances of resettlements and exiles to the Urals to, say, the artistry of the “depressive school” of Ural drama). This same conflictuality is also identified with the parameter of the geographical-territorial borderland: the junction of Europe and Asia. In this article, we will be interested in the geopoetic aspects of Andrei Rodionov and Ekaterina Troepolskaya’s play “Happiness Is Just Around the Corner”, included in the collection of poetic plays “Optimism” (2017). This text, in our opinion, develops these characteristics - in terms of the author’s, generic, and substantive positions and can be considered part of the “Ural text” of Russian literature.

title: A NARRATIVE ABOUT POETIC TALENT IN THE BOOK “PHILOSOPHY OF POETRY” BY V. KALPIDI
abstract: The article analyzes V. Kalpidi’s book “Philosophy of Poetry” (2019) as a transdiscursive philosophical ego-text. Calpidi’s work is defined as important for studying the evolution of modern Russian poetry, as it reflects the transition of writers to a meta-position in relation to their own work and the actualization of self-reflection. Calpidi, a metamodernist and cultural trader of the Urals, reflects in the Philosophy of Poetry the triad “gift-genius-talent” through the relationship of synchrony and diachrony: genius generates meanings, talent exposes them in “banality” to transform the recipient, erasing the boundaries of life and creativity. Transdiscursivity justifies his “right to speak” by deconstructing truisms for the circulation of meanings in the local literary community and among the field of poetry as a whole, which provides the generative potential of discourse. In Calpidi’s book The Philosophy of Poetry, the author is represented as the “center of coherence of discourses”: he forms not just a text, but a complex tradition with new acts of speech. title: ODE IN THE POETRY OF BORIS RYZSHY
abstract: The article is devoted to the problem of studying the odic tradition in the poetry of Boris Ryzhy. The genre of the ode and its Russian-language canon have already been studied in some detail at the level of pathos, stylistics, and verse practices. However, since Romanticism, the canon of the ode has been transformed, mandatory signs are violated, and the canon is replaced by the inner measure of the genre. At the same time, the issue of trends in genre change in the poetry of the twentieth century remains poorly understood. Practically nothing has been written about the odic tradition in Boris Ryzhy’s poetry, which is not at all surprising: firstly, Ryzhy himself is not very willing to give genre titles to poems, and secondly, his odic mode is clearly inferior to the elegiac. The subjectivity and imagery of Ryzhy’s texts also contradicts classical models. At the end of the twentieth century, the ode does not resemble its canonical invariant either stylistically or motifically, which may illustrate B.’s poem. title: STRONG POSITIONS OF PARATEX IN THE PLAY BY NIKOLAI KOLYADA “TWO DROPS OF “KOTY””
abstract: This article examines the strong paratextual positions in Nikolai Kolyada’s play “Two Drops of ‘Koti’.” The first strong paratextual position in this play is the author’s name, which shapes the reader’s expectations based on the playwright’s cultural reputation. The next strong position is the title, which, in terms of pre-understanding, requires some knowledge of what “Koti” is. Next comes the subtitle, which lacks a strict genre specification - “a play.” With this subtitle, the author leaves the reader (and the director) the right to determine the work’s genre, to read the play as they wish, or rather, as the text suggests, while the text suggests various genre versions of itself. Following the subtitle is a dedication referencing a real historical figure, Nadezhda Petrovna Lamanova, who turns out to be the play’s protagonist, as can be discerned from the next strong paratextual position - the cast list. This position in Kolyada’s play dictates a rather broad range of meanings, which are only concretized when referring to the text. title: THE USE OF THE MULTIPLATFORM SERVICES ANKI, QUIZLET AND MEMRISE IN TEACHING LEXIS: PROS AND CONS
abstract: An integral part of modern language learning and its study is digitalization: there are a huge number of resources for the development of all types of activities: speaking, listening, reading, writing.The article is devoted to such types of digital technologies as multi-platform applications using Flashcard Apps, their main goal is the expansion of vocabulary, effective memorization of vocabulary by integrating it into a long-playing memory. Cross-platform services Anki, Quizlet and Memrise are resources widely known in this segment, they are based on the “active recall” method in synthesis with the principle of spaced repetition. These digital tools are used by different categories of teachers and tutors in the learning process as auxiliary mechanisms that are applied as services to replenish the lexical reserve, better memorization of language units with minimal time costs. The implementation of such instruments also helps to develop the digital competencies of tutors. The second category of users involves those people who study languages themselves and use application for self-development.The study is based on the empirical method. title: RESEARCH ON THE PROCESS OF FORMING OF PRESCHOOLERS’ FOREIGN LANGUAGE COMMUNICATION CULTURE
abstract: This article presents a study addressing the challenge of developing foreign language communication skills using a second language in the context of personality development among preschool children. The paper proposes methodical foundations for this process while identifying four essential components-motivation, cognition, behavior, reflection - that facilitate effective preparation of children for intercultural communication. By systematizing these methodological elements, the study makes a substantial contribution toward comprehending and advancing early childhood education in multilingual settings. The research relies upon core principles of foreign language pedagogy, intercultural communication theory, and age-specific psychological insights. Utilized methods encompassed both theoretical approaches like comparative analyses and syntheses of relevant literature, alongside practical tools such as surveys, classroom experiments, and observation-based assessments. Data sources included scholarly publications, children’s activity outcomes, and experimental results derived from piloting the author-developed English curriculum ‘ABC Class,’ tailored specifically for preschool students.

title: COMPARISON OF THE EFFECTIVENESS OF TEAMAND INDIVIDUAL SPORTS FOR ADOLESCENTS’ SOCIALIZATION
abstract: This paper examines the role of team and individual sports in the socialization of adolescents. Theoretical foundations of socialization in sports are reviewed, and the psychological and social effects of participation in different types of sports by adolescents are analyzed. It is noted that team sports promote the development of communication skills, cooperation, and group identity, while individual sports mainly foster self-discipline and personal responsibility. Using an experimental study, a comparative analysis of the influence of participation in team and individual sports on adolescents’ socialization indicators (communication activity, self-esteem, level of social support, anxiety-depressive symptoms) is presented. The results showed that adolescents engaged in team sports have higher communication skills and social support compared to those in individual sports, who exhibited lower 1 self-esteem and higher anxiety tendencies. A table of the research results is provided. The conclusion is made that team sports are a more effective means of socializing adolescents compared to individual sports, but it is emphasized that individual differences should be taken into account. title: THE IMPRO FORUM AS A PLATFORM FOREX CHANGING EXPERIENCES AND IMPROVING THE QUALIFICATIONS OF MEDIA EDUCATORS
abstract: The first part of the article, “Creating an Educational Ecosystem for Media Educators,” describes the activities of the Chelyabinsk State University’s Media Education Research and Training Center, which coordinates work with youth media projects. Particular attention is paid to the need for a systematic approach to training media educators and the creation of the “Academic Year for Media Mentors” concept. The second part of the article, “Evolution and Contents of the ImPRO Forum,” is devoted to the center’s project, the ImPRO Forum, which has evolved from a local competition into a large-scale educational marathon since 2012. The structure of the forum (competition, educational platforms, Teleconference of journalism faculties), its development thanks to grant support, and specific events of the XI forum, including master classes, presentations of practices, and a media pedagogy laboratory, are described in detail. Particular attention is paid to the practical value of the forum for participants. The final part of the article, “Long-Term Educational Initiatives and Their Results,” tells about systemic projects that grew out of the ImPRO forum: advanced training courses, the Map of

title: SPECIFICS OF DEVELOPING PRESCHOOL CHILDREN’S AUTONOMOUS PERSONALITY WHILE LEARNING A FOREIGN LANGUAGE
abstract: This article explores the principal didactic challenges of fostering preschoolers’ autonomous development through foreign-language instruction. Its relevance stems from recent increases in intercultural integration and international cooperation, which have generated growing individual, societal, and governmental interest in foreign-language education. These trends underscore the critical importance of early childhood exposure to additional languages. Contemporary realities call for viewing the child as an equal partner in their own development and in intercultural communication. The study’s objective is to substantiate the potential for nurturing preschoolers’ autonomy via foreign-language means. The research reviews scientific approaches, methodologies, and theoretical frameworks proposed by leading Russian scholars-including N. D. Galskova, Z. N. Nikitenko, E. Yu. Protasova, N. M. Rodina, N.A. Gorlova, N. A. Tarasiuk, E. I. Negnevitskaia, A. M. Shakhnarovich, A. N. Utekhina, A. A. Leontiev, I. A. title: “EUGENE ONEGIN” BY A. S. PUSHKIN AS A BOOK HYPERTEXT:A PROJECT OF A DIGITAL EDUCATIONAL RESOURCE
abstract: The article presents a description of the project of a digital hypertext educational resource developed on the basis of the first chapter of the novel in verse by A. S. Pushkin “Eugene Onegin”. The purpose of the study is to demonstrate how the hypertext format can be used in the practice of teaching literature and how it helps to adapt a classical literary text to the educational needs of the modern generation of students. The theoretical basis is modern research in the field of methods of teaching literature and digital humanities, as well as the concept of hypertextuality of a literary text. The research methods include project design, structural and intertextual analysis, and commenting techniques. The result of the study is a digital educational resource implemented in the format of a PowerPoint presentation and structurally including the text of the chapter, a system of notes and comments, as well as thematic blocks. The target audience of the product are literature teachers, 9th-grade students completing their studies under the basic general education program, as well as students of philological faculties. title: VALUE PRIORITIES OF FIRST-YEARS STUDENTS AT ECONOMIC UNIVERSITY IN THE CONTEXT OF STUDYING THE DISCIPLINE «FOUNDATIONS OF RUSSIAN STATEHOOD»
abstract: Possible ways of solving one of the tasks of the educational course “Fundamentals of Russian statehood” are consideredthe formation of a personal value system of students and its correlation with the system of traditional values of Russian society. The effectiveness of appealing to personal values for shaping the worldview and civic position of future specialists is substantiated. Based on the analysis of the literature, an algorithm for the formation of the personal hierarchy of values of the student is formulated. The data of the study of the value system of first-year students of the university, conducted in 2023-2024 on the basis of the Institute of Economics of Nizhny Novgorod State University, obtained as part of the teaching of the discipline “Fundamentals of Russian Statehood”, are presented. The research used the methodology and questionnaire of M. Rokich. This technique is one of the most popular tools for studying values, widely used in psychology, sociology and marketing. The basic idea is that values are the main guidelines in people’s lives and influence their behavior, decision-making and attitude towards various aspects of social reality. title: SMART EDUCATION IN CONTEMPORARY CULTURE
abstract: The fourth technological revolution, being the main driver of smart technology development, contributed to the launch of the processes of digitalisation and smartisation, which contributed to the formation and development of a new form of being of mankind - smart culture, forming a smart society and with it a smart person. These processes and phenomena are certainly reflected in the education sector. The paradigm ‘smart’, affecting the modern educational space, has triggered a change of fundamentals, which critically changes the educational pace and existing practices. The article investigates the essence of the concept of smart education as a subject of a new form of culture. The definition and classification of the structural complex of the adaptable smart-educational model is given. Explication of the essence of smart-education as a subject of smart culture allows the author to talk about priority educational results, which will be expressed not only in the formation of schoolchildren’s correct attitude to smart technologies and smart devices, but also in solving the problems arising in this case.

title: THE PRINCIPLES OF INTERCONNECTED TEACHING OF FOREIGN LANGUAGES AT THE HIGHER EDUCATIONAL INSTITUTION
abstract: The article analyzes the principles of interconnected teaching of foreign languages at higher educational institutions. Based on the research of domestic scientists, the author considers the process of teaching several foreign languages in coordination with teaching the native language of students. The importance of building a holistic system in the study of foreign languages, taking into account the native language, based on a set of methodological principles is emphasized. Considering that the native language has a significant impact on the process of learning foreign languages, and the study of the second foreign language occurs under the influence of the previously studied first foreign language, the author focuses on the consciously comparative method of co-studying languages, which allows minimizing negative interlingual interference that causes errors in speech, and enhancing positive interlingual interference, simplifying the acquisition of languages. title: METHODICAL RECOMMENDATIONS FOR THE USE OF MIND MAPS FOR THE DEVELOPMENT OF ORAL PROFESSIONAL COMMUNICATION
abstract: The development of oral professional communication at a university level is a complex task that requires the integration of speech, cognitive, and professional components. Today’s labor market demands that graduates not only possess knowledge of specialized vocabulary but also be able to engage effectively in foreign-language professional interactions, articulate well-founded opinions, participate in dialogues, and discuss professional issues. Enhancing these skills involves incorporating approaches into the educational process that facilitate structured mastery of language material. One such tool is mind mapping, which offers significant potential for systematizing information, visual planning, and developing productive foreign-language communication skills. This article provides methodological recommendations for using mind maps to organize logical statements, develop speech skills, and solve problem situations. title: ORGANIZATION OF ACTIVITIES OF MANAGEMENT TEAMS OF INNOVATIVE EDUCATIONAL ORGANIZATIONS
abstract: The article discusses the importance of forming management teams in a comprehensive educational organization. It is noted that in most comprehensive educational organizations there is a decline in the quality of education due to the ineffectiveness of decisions made by the head, as well as the failure to use the potential for forming management teams to develop and make decisions. At the same time, it is proven that the formation of creative teams, work teams, and management teams levels out situations of making incorrect and ineffective management decisions and, as a result, delays in the process of improving the quality of education. The authors highlight the need to create teams that would develop strategic goals, solve urgent problems in a short time, develop and implement innovative practices, and take responsibility for management decisions. Examples of various types and kinds of management teams formed for specific tasks with different compositions are given. The purpose of the study is to justify the formation of management teams for specific urgent tasks of a general education organization. title: DEVELOPMENT OF PEDAGOGICAL REFLECTION POTENTIAL
abstract: Reflection is one of the promising areas of research in modern humanities. This article explores the historical dynamics of understanding and researching the phenomenon of reflection in the context of psychological and pedagogical thought from ancient times to the present day, and highlights the importance of incorporating reflective activities into the modern educational process. The relevance of this research is driven by several factors. Firstly, the current demands on professionals, which include continuous professional growth, self-education, and lifelong learning, necessitate active reflection. Secondly, the limited knowledge and insufficient development of reflection skills at all levels of the educational system. The pedagogical potential of reflection has historical roots that go back to the philosophical ideas of the ancient era. Since the 20th century, psychology has proposed numerous reflective techniques and practices that have become widely used in educational settings. In today’s educational environment, reflection has gained significant importance. title: OPPORTUNITIES OF THE ACADEMIC SUBJECT “PHYSICAL EDUCATION” FOR THE FORMATION OF PHYSICAL FITNESS AND HEALTH MOTIVATION IN ADOLESCENTS WITH DISABILITIES
abstract: This article examines the potential of the academic subject “Physical Education” for fostering sustainable physical culture and health-related motivation among adolescents with disabilities. The first part of the article discusses the opportunities offered by person-centered, adaptive, and competency-based approaches that consider the individual physical, medical, and psychoemotional characteristics of the adolescents. The person-centered approach relies on program-individualization, the creation of “success situations,” and reflective practices, which contribute to enhanced self-esteem and intrinsic motivation. The adaptive approach encompasses physical rehabilitation, social integration, psychoemotional correction, and cognitive development, employing methods such as hydrotherapy, Paralympic sports, art therapy, and VR simulators. The competency-based approach aims to develop key competencies in adolescents, including health-preserving, communicative, cognitive, reflective, and socially adaptive skills, thus promoting long-term engagement in physical education. title: GAMIFICATION OF EDUCATION: ANALYSIS OF EXPERIENCE AND CRITIQUE
abstract: This article explores the challenges of integrating gamification into educational disciplines and ways to overcome them. It analyses recently published systematic reviews on the gamification of education, concluding that gamification in education significantly increases student motivation and engagement, particularly in e-learning, and helps overcome anxiety in foreign language learning. However, many studies have been criticized due to shortcomings in applied research and a weak connection to theoretical foundations. To implement gamification successfully, teachers must have a thorough understanding of its theories and the necessary resources. The article emphasizes the importance of understanding gamification theory for teachers to assess the advantages and disadvantages of its use in the classroom. The article summarizes the experience of using gamification in English language classes at a university. The article also addresses the challenges faced by teachers in gamifying education, including the deteriorating quality of digital platform services, students’ reluctance to cope with the boredom of routine work, and the increasing workload of teachers. title: ISSUES OF EDUCATIONAL MOTIVATION AND WAYS TO SOLVE THEM
abstract: The article describes the problems of students’ motivation towards high-quality knowledge, universal learning activities, functional literacy; presents facts confirming parents’ and teachers’ concerns about low educational motivation; outlines a plan developed by the teaching staff aimed at addressing this issue. Additionally, it clarifies the working definition of educational motivation based on materials from Peterson L. G., Anisimova O. S., and Agapov Y. V. It provides justification for specific tasks that have been solved or are yet to be addressed by the pedagogical team of MAOU “School No. 104 of Chelyabinsk.” The connection between setting goals and objectives with previous work as part of a Regional Innovative Platform and Federal Innovative Platform related to formative criterion-based assessment and activity-based learning technology of the Center for System-Activity Pedagogy “School 2000...” is demonstrated. The article also identifies challenges, reasons for difficulties faced by teachers in fostering motivation, and highlights demotivators. title: MEDIA COMPETENCIES AS A MEANS OF INTERACTION WITH THE MEMORATIVE LANDSCAPE (THE CASE OF ARKAIM)
abstract: The article examines the manifestation of visitors’ media competencies at the Arkaim Museum-Reserve through photography practices and interaction with the memorative landscape. The empirical basis of the study includes data from a visitor survey conducted during expeditions in 2023-2024, supplemented by thick descriptions from participant observation. The methodology incorporates visual analysis of photographs of Arkaim, correlated with respondents’ answers. The aim of the work is to identify how media competencies are manifested and curtailed in a sacred space.The analysis reveals that visitors’ media practices are predominantly personal rather than communicative. Photography serves as a tool for reflection and preservation of an emotional connection to the place, rather than for creating content for subsequent publication and dissemination. Respondents’ visual attention is focused on panoramic natural objects (mountains, steppe, sunrises), rather than archaeological or social scenes.
